newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 16.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

In a move to encourage commuters to leave their cars at home or change from the overcrowded tube, bus fares are being frozen or cut. In a calculated gamble London Transport chiefs are increasing tube fares by up to four times the rate of inflation on some routes, to persuade more people to use the bus.

Goldman Sachs, Wall Street's last remaining big partnership, named 125 executives to managing director positions last night, several dozen of them based in London. The new positions are a response to defections from Goldman Sachs to other banks.

The chief executive of BAA, Sir John Egan, is expected to tell the Aviation Club of Great Britain that he will accept the principle of a limit on car parking spaces if a green light is given for the construction of a fifth terminal at Heathrow.
POUND MAKES ITS MARK WITH 21-MONTH HIGH

The pound reached a 21-month high of 2.4460 against the Deutschmark, powered by booming British stock markets, stronger oil prices and the government's non-committal approach to European monetary union.

The Sultan of Brunei is believed to be on the verge of buying the Hyde Park Hotel from Granada Group for 90 million stg, 25 million stg more than its book value. The Sultan already owns the Dorchester and the Bel Air in Beverly Hills.
CHINA'S DATANG HEADS FOR LISTING IN LONDON

It is hoped that a long delayed signing by SIB chairman Sir Andrew Large of a Sino-British memo of understanding on securities will clear the way for the listing of Beijing Datang Power on the London stock market as early as next month. Sponsor of the first listing of a Chinese company on the London stock market Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, is keen to see trading by the end of the year.
REFORM CALL TO CHANCELLOR ON SHARE BUYBACKS

Britain's multinational companies in areas of banking, utilities, pharmaceuticals and media groups are putting pressure on Chancellor Kenneth Clarke for further tax reform following his decision to cancel tax benefits linked to share repurchases.
